newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLD FIELDS SAYS TAVISTOCK OFFER REJECTED.
newsitem.headline: GOLD FIELDS SAYS TAVISTOCK OFFER REJECTED.

text.p: Mining house Gold Fields of South Africa said on Tuesday JCI Ltd's unlisted coal unit Tavistock Collieries Ltd had rejected its 1.5 billion rand bid in favour of another offer.

"Gold Fields Coal...received written communication from Tavistock Collieries Ltd informing Gold Fields Coal that it did not intend taking further (its) offer to purchase the coal business of JCI Ltd," Gold Fields said in a statement.
Gold Fields Coal chairman Barbara Day said a figure of 1.5 billion rand quoted in the press as the amount offered by Gold Fields for JCI's coal assets was an accurate representation of its bid.
Tavistock's chief executive told Gold Fields in a letter it was pursuing an alternative offer, Gold Fields said.
Analysts have speculated an alternative JCI might take would be to merge Tavistock with Lonrho Plc as part of its planned purchase of 26.8 percent of the British group.
Gold Fields' Day said she was surprised by the rejection considering the companies had been in discussions for some time.

"I am on record as saying that Gold Fields Coal would be willing to pay a substantial cash price for Tavistock and that our offer would be subject to revision up or down following a due dilligence study," she added.
Day said it had informed JCI it was open to further discussions.
The firm said previously that it would have considered restructuring Gold Fields Coal, if the bid had proved successful.
JCI was not immediately available for comment.
